title: Is Every Answer Right?
subtitle: Learn to check facts against a source.
objectives: Identify claims that are directly supported by a given source.
Correct claims that contradict information found in a source.
State when a source does not provide information for a specific claim.

scenes.title: Think About It!
scenes.narration: Imagine someone tells you something important, like when your favorite club meets. How do you know if it's true? Do you just believe them, or do you check?
scenes.visualAction: A cartoon character looks confused, then a thought bubble appears with a question mark and a document icon.

scenes.title: Check Your Sources
scenes.narration: It's super important to check information against its original source. A confident answer isn't always a correct answer. We need to find the exact words that support what's being said.
scenes.visualAction: Two cartoon characters, one holding a paper with a statement, the other holding a different paper, comparing them closely.

scenes.title: Library Club Mystery
scenes.narration: Let's look at an example. We have an announcement for the Cloud Library Club. Someone made a list of details about it. We'll compare their list to the actual announcement.
scenes.visualAction: A cartoon character points to a digital display showing the 'Cloud Library Club Announcement' material.

scenes.title: What We Found
scenes.narration: The announcement clearly states the club meets on Tuesday, not Wednesday, and requires booking. It doesn't mention snacks at all. If a source is silent, we can't guess. We must say we don't know and ask the source directly.
scenes.visualAction: The display highlights the corrected parts of the announcement and shows a '?' for snacks.

scenes.title: Be a Fact-Checker
scenes.narration: Being a good fact-checker means you don't just accept information. You actively look for proof. If you can't find it, or if it contradicts the source, you point it out. This helps everyone get the right information.
scenes.visualAction: A magnifying glass icon hovers over a document, then a checkmark appears.

scenes.title: Your Turn to Check
scenes.narration: Now it's your turn! I'll give you a new source and some claims. Your job is to compare each claim to the source and correct any mistakes. If the source doesn't say, you say so!
scenes.visualAction: A cartoon character presents a new document and a list of claims, gesturing for the learner to begin.

scenes.title: Great Job!
scenes.narration: You've learned a super important skill today: how to check claims against a source. This helps you understand what's true, what's false, and what's unknown. Keep practicing, and you'll be a master fact-checker!
scenes.visualAction: A cartoon character gives a thumbs-up, and a 'Well Done!' badge appears on screen.

reading.title: The Importance of Sources
reading.text: A source is where information comes from. When someone makes a claim, it's vital to check if their claim matches the original source. Don't just trust a confident tone; look for the exact words in the source that support or contradict the claim. Being a good fact-checker means always verifying information.

reading.title: How to Compare Claims
reading.text: The example answer says Wednesday, but the announcement says Tuesday. It says no booking, but the source requires advance booking. Snacks are not mentioned, so this source cannot confirm whether they are provided.

reading.title: What if the Source is Silent?
reading.text: Sometimes, a claim is made, but your source doesn't have any information about it. In this case, you cannot say the claim is true or false based on that source. The correct answer is to state that the information is not provided by the source. You might then ask the original source for clarification.

materials.title: Invented library source
materials.text: Invented Cloud Library Club announcement: the activity is on Tuesday from 4 PM to 6 PM. Entry is free. Advance booking is required. The announcement says nothing about snacks.

materials.title: Authored answer to check
materials.text: An authored practice answer containing mistakes: 'The activity is on Wednesday at 4 PM. No booking is needed, and free snacks are provided.'

materials.title: Invented museum source
materials.text: Invented museum announcement: visits are on Saturday from 10 AM to noon. Advance booking is required. The announcement says nothing about student discounts.

promptExamples.initial: Tell me about the Cloud Library Club.
promptExamples.improved: Using the Cloud Library Club announcement, tell me the meeting day, time, and if booking is required. Also, mention if snacks are provided.
promptExamples.followup: Can you show me the exact text in the announcement that confirms the club meets on Wednesday and provides snacks?

activity.title: Check the library answer
activity.instructions: Compare each claim with the announcement. Correct the day and booking requirement, and identify what the announcement cannot confirm. Quote the source phrase that supports each correction.
activity.starter:
Invented Cloud Library Club announcement: the activity is on Tuesday from 4 PM to 6 PM. Entry is free. Advance booking is required. The announcement says nothing about snacks.
An authored practice answer containing mistakes: 'The activity is on Wednesday at 4 PM. No booking is needed, and free snacks are provided.'
activity.expectedEvidence: Correct day, correct booking requirement, unknown snack status and supporting phrases.

quiz.question: According to the 'Cloud Library Club Announcement', what is the correct meeting day?
quiz.explanation: The announcement clearly states: 'Meeting every Tuesday from 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM.'

quiz.question: The library announcement says nothing about snacks. What can you conclude?
options: The announcement cannot confirm snack availability.
quiz.explanation: A missing mention does not establish presence or absence. For a real event, ask the responsible organiser.

quiz.question: The claim says Wednesday, but the announcement says Tuesday. Which source phrase supports your correction?
quiz.explanation: Use the phrase about the day itself, rather than an unrelated detail from the same source.

mission.title: Check a museum claim
mission.instructions: Authored claim: 'The museum opens on Sunday from 10 AM to noon, no booking is needed, and there are student discounts.' Compare it with the museum announcement in the lesson materials. Correct the claim using source evidence and identify the detail the source cannot confirm.
rubric: Saturday, 10 AM to noon is stated.
The correction cites the supplied source and adds no invented facts.

hints.question: How do I know if a claim is true?
hints.answer: You need to find the exact words in the source material that support the claim. If you can't find them, or if the source says something different, the claim might be incorrect or unconfirmed.

hints.question: What if the source doesn't talk about a specific detail?
hints.answer: If the source doesn't mention a detail, you cannot confirm it. You should state that the information is not provided by the source. Don't guess or assume!

hints.question: My friend sounds very sure. Should I still check?
hints.answer: Yes, always check! A confident tone doesn't mean the information is correct. Good fact-checkers always verify information against the original source, no matter how confident someone sounds.

imageBrief.title: Comparing Claims to Sources
imageBrief.scenario: A student is comparing a written claim about a museum's operating hours and booking requirements with an official museum flyer.
imageBrief.composition: A split screen or side-by-side view. On the left, a cartoon student character holds a paper with a handwritten note. On the right, a clear, colorful cartoon flyer for 'History Makers Museum'. The student is looking back and forth between the two documents.

History Makers Museum Flyer: 'Open Saturday, 10 AM - 12 PM. Booking Required. Free parking.'

The flyer says 'Open Saturday, 10 AM - 12 PM. Booking Required. Free parking.' A magnifying glass and checkmark icon suggest fact-checking.

educatorNotes.sampleAnswer: Library: Tuesday, 4–6 PM; free entry; advance booking required; snacks unconfirmed. Museum: Saturday, 10 AM–noon; advance booking required; student discounts unconfirmed. Compare only with the supplied invented cards.
educatorNotes.commonMisconception: Students often assume that if a piece of information isn't contradicted by a source, it must be true, even if the source doesn't mention it. They may also be swayed by the confidence of the person making the claim rather than checking the source itself.
reviewChecks: Saturday, 10 AM to noon is stated.
The correction cites the supplied source and adds no invented facts.
educatorNotes.safetyNotes: This lesson involves comparing information. Remind students that when checking real-world information, they should always use reliable, official sources (like a school website for school hours) and, if unsure, ask a trusted adult.
